question: A very distant source of light produces nearly plane wavefronts near the observer. Explain why.

options.A: A distant source produces spherical wavefronts of very large radius. Over a small region near the observer, the curvature of such a large-radius sphere is negligible, so the wavefront appears nearly plane.
options.B: A distant source produces plane wavefronts because light ceases to spread in all directions.
options.C: A distant source produces cylindrical wavefronts because the observer is far from it.
options.D: A distant source produces no wavefront because its light intensity is low.
